text: Correct: a field extension has dimension one exactly when its scalar embedding is surjective; here that embedding is the constants map into the actual residue field. This is the rational-place definition in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Injectivity is automatic for the field map. No finite-dimensional premise is missing: infinite-dimensional finrank is zero, so cannot satisfy degree=1. The published infinity evaluation proves surjectivity concretely, while the native X²+1 place has degree two under its irreducibility hypothesis. These controls distinguish rational from nonrational places. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L525).
The published rational-function computation supplies a constant residue at infinity, including zero and negative-degree functions.
The actual irreducible X²+1 place has degree two, so the degree-one criterion does not collapse all places.

Correct: at a degree-one place, the constants map k→F_P is bijective and becomes a k-algebra equivalence. This is the residue-field interpretation of rational places in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The definition uses that specific map, so its inverse recovers constant residue values rather than choosing an unrelated field isomorphism. Degree one is retained; a quadratic residue field is excluded. The published infinity equivalence is defined through this constructor, and its application theorem sends each constant to its actual residue. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L562).
The source proves degree one for the native infinity place using the actual constant-residue calculation.
The published infinity equivalence sends every constant to its actual residue, via the general degree-one equivalence.

Correct: the degree-one residue equivalence evaluates a constant by the existing algebra map k→F_P. Its construction wraps this bijective map without changing its values, which is the canonical constants inclusion of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The equality specifies the direction of the equivalence and rules out an unintended automorphism of the base field. Zero and one are included automatically. The published infinity application equation uses this theorem directly; the result makes no claim that every place has degree one. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L569).
The published infinity equivalence sends every constant to its actual residue, via the general degree-one equivalence.

Correct: the scalar map into the residue field factors through the valuation ring and then reduction, the quotient construction in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean permits a commutative semiring R because the equality needs only compatible algebra maps, not additive inverses in R. `IsScalarTower` is essential: it identifies the given R-actions with that composite. No injectivity of R is assumed or needed. The published polynomial-residue calculation uses this same constants reduction to identify the residue with the polynomial's constant coefficient. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L494).
The existing residue computation reduces a polynomial evaluated at a residue-zero element to its constant coefficient.

Correct: reduction modulo the maximal ideal is zero exactly for elements of that ideal, characterized multiplicatively by v(f)<1. This is the residue map of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The docstring's positive valuation means positive additive order away from zero; Lean's displayed multiplicative inequality has the reversed orientation. Zero is included correctly because v(0)=0<1. The published polynomial-residue computation evaluates at such residue-zero elements, and the native infinity uniformizer supplies the positive-order control. No extraneous nonzero premise is needed here. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L502).
The existing residue computation reduces a polynomial evaluated at a residue-zero element to its constant coefficient.
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.

Correct: a nonzero regular function reduces to zero exactly when it has strictly positive order. This is the maximal-ideal criterion underlying [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The nonzero hypothesis is essential under ord(0)=0: zero has zero residue but would fail the strict order inequality. The source derives the statement through the actual residue kernel and maximal ideal. The native X⁻¹ uniformizer has order one at infinity, while the published polynomial-residue calculation uses this vanishing condition to reduce evaluations to constant terms. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L507).
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.
The existing residue computation reduces a polynomial evaluated at a residue-zero element to its constant coefficient.

Correct: within the valuation ring, the maximal ideal consists of elements whose multiplicative value is strictly below one, as in [Stacks, Lemma 10.50.16](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). This includes zero and excludes units of value one. Lean's subtype supplies regularity, so the criterion concerns the actual local ring rather than arbitrary nonunits of F. Its residue-zero theorem identifies this ideal with the quotient-map kernel. The native infinity uniformizer verifies the normalized positive-order side; no function-field finiteness hypothesis is required. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L411).
The published residue-kernel theorem uses this exact maximal-ideal characterization.
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.

Correct: for a nonzero element of O(P), membership in its maximal ideal is equivalent to positive additive order, as in [Stacks, Lemma 10.50.16](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). Lean explicitly excludes zero because its assigned order is zero despite belonging to the ideal. The strict inequality separates nonunits from order-zero units and has the correct sign. The published residue-vanishing theorem consumes this criterion, while X⁻¹ at infinity has order one. Thus both the algebraic ideal and normalized valuation interpretations use the same carrier. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L422).
The source derives the actual nonzero residue-vanishing characterization from this ideal criterion.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: for nonzero f, v(f)=exp(−ord(f)); comparison with one therefore gives v(f)<1 exactly when ord(f)>0. This matches the maximal-ideal convention in [Stacks, Lemma 10.50.16](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). The result is stated in F, so regularity follows rather than being assumed. The nonzero guard prevents the false zero-input equivalence 0<1 iff 0<0. The published infinity formulas identify v∞ with exp(intDegree) and give ord∞(X⁻¹)=1, checking the sign on an actual place. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L415).
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.
The native infinity computation equates valuation below one with negative rational-function degree, matching positive additive order.

Correct: a nonzero element of the valuation ring is a unit exactly when its additive order is zero, the unit criterion in [Stacks, Lemma 10.50.16](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8). The subtype ensures regularity, and the nonzero premise is essential because ord(0)=0 would otherwise classify zero as a unit. The source first uses the multiplicative value-one criterion, then translates through exp(−ord). The published uniformizer decomposition actually obtains its unit factor by this argument. No global function-field hypothesis or choice of uniformizer appears in the equivalence itself. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L396).
The published uniformizer decomposition produces a unit by showing the normalized quotient has order zero and is nonzero.
The existing multiplicative criterion is the exact source comparison used in this additive version.

Correct: a normalized place has a nontrivial surjective integer value group, so some element has valuation above one and lies outside O(P). Thus its valuation subring is proper, as required by [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.4](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). This uses normalization rather than assuming all valuation rings are proper: a trivially valued field would be an exception. The published rational-coordinate calculation gives the explicit excluded element X at infinity. No global function-field or exact-constants hypothesis is needed once a normalized place has been supplied. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L426).
The actual rational coordinate is outside the valuation ring precisely at infinity, checking the regular/pole distinction.

Correct: the only valuation overrings of a discrete valuation ring in its fraction field are itself and the field. The larger ring here is proper because it also comes from a normalized place. Equality of rings therefore gives P=Q, matching [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.13(d)](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean obtains the dimension-one restriction from the DVR instance and explicitly uses Q.integers≠⊤. This is not valid for arbitrary higher-rank valuations. [Target provenance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/commit/8d9c982bc5c3f1d901fec809d860d058bcf5da38) identifies the publishing account as an author of the current implementation. The native X test distinguishes finite places from infinity. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L448).
The actual rational coordinate is outside the valuation ring precisely at infinity, checking the regular/pole distinction.
The actual properness theorem rules out the full-field overring in the source proof.

Correct: equivalent valuations determine the same normalized place, and equal places have equivalent valuations by reflexivity. This is the normalized correspondence in [Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.1.13](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Surjectivity onto the fixed integer value group removes the rescaling ambiguity that would remain for arbitrary valuations. The source retains both directions rather than equating equivalence with pointwise equality without normalization. The published valuation-ring injectivity proof uses this identification, and the native X-membership theorem separates the finite-place rings from the infinity ring. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L438).
Equal valuation rings give equivalent normalized valuations and hence the same place in the published proof.
The actual rational coordinate is outside the valuation ring precisely at infinity, checking the regular/pole distinction.

Correct: every integer is realized by a nonzero function at a normalized discrete place, the surjectivity convention in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean strengthens raw surjectivity by excluding the junk witness zero. Its proof replaces a zero witness by one; that branch can occur only for target order zero. Positive and negative orders are both allowed. The published infinity uniformizer has order one, and the actual integer-power order laws provide the expected normalization. The assertion is existential and does not claim a canonical function for each order. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L247).
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: the place's normalized multiplicative valuation reaches every nonzero integer exponent, so its additive order reaches every integer, matching [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The sign change in ord does not affect surjectivity. Lean allows the witness for order zero to be zero; its separate strengthened theorem supplies a nonzero witness when required. The native X⁻¹ uniformizer at infinity has order one, so this is not surjectivity onto a proper subgroup or only nonnegative orders. No global function-field assumption is needed. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L244).
The published sharpening replaces any zero witness at order zero by one, establishing the stronger nonzero realization.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: a nonzero summand of uniquely least order cannot cancel in a finite sum, by the strict triangle principle in [Stichtenoth, Lemma 1.1.11](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean requires j∈s and f(j)≠0, excluding empty sums and a spurious distinguished zero. Other zero terms cause no cancellation; because ord(0)=0, the displayed inequality may impose a stronger condition on them than the extended-valuation convention, but remains sufficient. The published companion theorem computes the sum's order under the same hypotheses. No assumption that the whole index type is finite is needed. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L272).
The existing companion source theorem computes the order of this actual finite sum as the distinguished summand order under the same guarded hypotheses.

Correct: division of two nonzero functions subtracts their orders, the quotient form of the valuation law in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Both nonzero hypotheses are necessary under totalized division and ord(0)=0: division by zero or a zero numerator would otherwise force a generally false order equality. The source derives subtraction from multiplication and inverse order. The published coefficient-normalization theorem uses this exact formula to turn least order into integral ratios, handling zero numerators separately. Negative orders and poles remain available. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L189).
The source explicitly splits zero coefficients, then applies ord_div only to nonzero numerator and minimizing denominator.

Correct: inversion negates the order, as for the valuation group in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Unlike multiplication of unrelated elements, this formula also survives Lean's totalization at zero: 0⁻¹=0 and −ord(0)=0. Thus the absence of a nonzero premise is intentional and sound. The published infinity-uniformizer proof applies this theorem to X⁻¹ and obtains order one from ord∞X=−1. For ordinary nonzero functions it exchanges zeros and poles without changing the normalized magnitude. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L178).
The existing native infinity place has the explicit uniformizer X⁻¹, with its normalized order computed in the proof.
The actual inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, checking the normalization.

Correct: an integer power multiplies the additive order by its exponent, extending the valuation law of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html) to negative powers. Lean correctly includes f=0: for nonzero exponents its totalized power is zero, and for exponent zero it is one; both have order zero. Consequently no nonzero guard is needed for this particular identity. The published native family cXᵃ(X−1)ᵇ computes its orders using these actual integer powers, retaining nonzero guards only where multiplication requires them. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L181).
The actual rational-function family cXᵃ(X−1)ᵇ has order −(a+b) at infinity for nonzero c.

Correct: taking a natural-number power multiplies order by that exponent, the repeated-product law in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.9](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean casts n into Z explicitly. The zero-function and zero-exponent cases remain valid under ord(0)=ord(1)=0, so no nonzero premise is necessary. The published Weierstrass-coordinate proof actually applies this theorem to x², y² and x³ while computing the required monomial orders. The statement concerns normalized integer order and does not introduce a sign change or a degree-of-field-extension factor. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L185).
The existing source explicitly computes orders of x², xy and x³ with ord_pow and ord_mul in its six-monomial Weierstrass calculation.

The map is x↦x⊗1: tensor the identity with the unit and use the inverse right-unit isomorphism. Both factors are actual bialgebra morphisms in [Mathlib](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Hom.lean#L346), so the construction preserves multiplication, counit and comultiplication. The published [evaluation and retraction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L57) confirm the intended inclusion. No antipode, field assumption or commutativity of either factor is needed.
The actual left map sends x to x⊗1.
The two published left maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.

The map is y↦1⊗y: tensor the unit with the identity and precompose the inverse left-unit isomorphism. [Mathlib’s unit and tensor maps](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L71) preserve both algebra and coalgebra structures. The published [evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L61) and right retraction check its orientation. This is valid over a commutative semiring with possibly noncommutative bialgebra factors; no antipode is used.
The actual right map sends y to1⊗y.
The two published right maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.

Evaluating the [actual inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L43) first gives x⊗1 in H₁⊗R and then applies the unit to its second factor. Hence the displayed value is x⊗1 in H₁⊗H₂, exactly the natural-language formula. [Mathlib’s tensor-map equation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L76) fixes the factor order. Zero and unit inputs follow the same formula, and the published retraction confirms the left factor is retained.
The two published left maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.

The inverse left-unit map sends y to 1⊗y; tensoring the unit on the first factor keeps precisely that value in H₁⊗H₂. This matches the [source definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L50) and [Mathlib’s left-unit formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L133). The scalar unit is not inserted in the right factor. The published right retraction confirms that projecting back recovers y, including zero.
The two published right maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.

Forgetting the coalgebra fields leaves the algebra homomorphism x↦x⊗1. The published [pointwise equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L57) proves equality with Mathlib’s algebra inclusion by extensionality. This is consistent with [Mathlib’s tensor-map forgetful equation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L85): packaging coalgebra compatibility adds proofs, not a different underlying map. The statement asserts equality of actual algebra homomorphisms over the same base, without requiring either factor commutative.
The actual left map sends x to x⊗1.

Both algebra homomorphisms send every y to 1⊗y, as the [published evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L61) shows. Extensionality therefore identifies the underlying algebra map of the bialgebra inclusion with the standard right inclusion. [Mathlib’s forgetful tensor-map equation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L85) uses the same convention. No carrier transport or opposite algebra is hidden, and noncommutative factors remain permitted.
The actual right map sends y to1⊗y.

Tensoring id with the counit and applying the right-unit isomorphism sends x⊗y to ε(y)•x. That is the stated projection. The [counit is itself a bialgebra morphism](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Hom.lean#L351), so the construction preserves both structures over a commutative semiring. Its published [pure-tensor equation and retraction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L91) pass. In particular it contracts the second factor using ε; it does not simply discard y.
The left projection contracts the second factor by its counit.
The two published left maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.

Apply the counit to the first factor, then the left-unit isomorphism: x⊗y maps to ε(x)•y. [Mathlib’s counit morphism](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Hom.lean#L351) and tensor map justify the bialgebra structure. The published [pure-tensor equation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L97) and right retraction verify this orientation and ε(1)=1. No cocommutativity or antipode assumption is needed, because the map uses only the counit.
The right projection contracts the first factor by its counit.
The two published right maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.

The [projection definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L77) maps x⊗y to x⊗ε(y), and the right-unit isomorphism evaluates that tensor as ε(y)•x. Thus the displayed scalar action matches the natural-language contraction exactly. [Mathlib’s right-unit equation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L156) supplies this normalization. When ε(y)=0 the result vanishes, and y=1 recovers x through the published retraction. No invertibility hypothesis is missing.
The two published left maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.

The first tensor factor is evaluated by ε, giving ε(x)⊗y, and the left-unit isomorphism turns that into ε(x)•y. This is precisely the [defined right projection](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L84), with [Mathlib’s left-unit convention](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean#L130). The published right retraction checks x=1, while x=0 yields zero. Arbitrary semiring bialgebras suffice; no antipode or chosen basis enters the equation.
The two published right maps compose to the identity, using ε(1)=1.
